title: Zariski local affine etale atlases of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There is a set-indexed Zariski covering $X=\bigcup_iX_i$ by open subspaces such that each $X_i$ admits a representable surjective etale morphism $h_{U_i}\to X_i$ with $U_i$ an affine scheme. Moreover each $X_i\to S$ factors through an affine open subscheme of $S$. Here an open subspace is a subfunctor whose inclusion is representable and becomes an open immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-open-immersion], and a Zariski covering means that their underlying open subsets cover the field-valued point classes of $X$. A field-valued point class means a map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ with $K$ a field, with two such maps identified when they agree over a common field extension; the underlying set of an open subspace is the set of classes that factor through it.

source.place: Tag 03FY (lemma-union-of-quasi-compact), including the final affine-base clause.

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas $p:h_V\to X$ that is representable, surjective and etale, using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For each $v\in V$, choose an affine open $W_v\subseteq S$ containing its image, and then an affine open $U_v\subseteq V$ containing $v$ and contained in the inverse image of $W_v$. Both choices follow from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Thus the $U_v$ cover $V$, and each structural map $U_v\to S$ factors through the open subscheme $W_v$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. The index set $I=|V|$ is a set within [def-weil-size-convention]; if $V$ is empty, use the empty family. Write $U_i,W_i$ for these choices.

source.place: Tag 03FY, first proof sentence; expand Tag 03FX (lemma-cover-by-union-affines), proof lines 710-715, before forming the unnecessary coproduct.

proof.text: For each $i$, the composite $f_i:h_{U_i}\to h_V\to X$ is representable and etale. Indeed, for a scheme test $h_T\to X$, representability of $p$ gives the scheme $P=T\times_XV$, with etale projection $P\to T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By pasting of fibre products, $T\times_XU_i=P\times_VU_i$, and its projection to $P$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]: the inverse-image open subscheme of $P$ under $P\to V$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its projection to $T$ is therefore an open immersion followed by an etale morphism; clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] make it etale. This verifies the required property on every scheme test.

source.place: Tag 03FX, proof lines 715-722: etale composition, applied separately to each affine piece.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-etale-scheme-map-open-image] to each $f_i$. It produces an open subspace $X_i\subseteq X$ with $|X_i|=\operatorname{im}(|U_i|\to|X|)$ and a representable surjective etale map $h_{U_i}\to X_i$. These open subspaces cover: given a field-valued point $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_XV$ surjects onto $\operatorname{Spec}K$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Choose a point of this nonempty scheme and its residue field $L$. The resulting map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$ has its image in some $U_i$, so factors through that open subscheme by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its composite to $X$ is the extension of $x$ to $L$, and hence represents the same point class. That class belongs to $|X_i|$. Thus $|X|=\bigcup_i|X_i|$, exactly the covering condition in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03FY, middle proof sentences, lines 738-742; Tag 06NF for the open-image factorization.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and a scheme test $h_T\to X_i$. For each $t\in T$, base change the surjective map $h_{U_i}\to X_i$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to X_i$. By the scheme-test definition of surjectivity [def-trf-algebraic-space] this is a nonempty scheme. A point and its residue field give an extension $L/\kappa(t)$ and a lift $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U_i$. Since $U_i\to S$ factors through $W_i$, the image of $t$ under $T\to S$ lies in $W_i$. Consequently $T\to S$ has image contained in $W_i$ and factors uniquely through the open subscheme $W_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] [def-weil-open-immersion]. For varying $T\to X_i$ these factorizations commute with pullback by uniqueness. They therefore define a natural transformation $X_i\to h_{W_i}$ whose composite with $h_{W_i}\to h_S$ is the structural map. This proves the affine-base clause for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 03FY, last proof sentence, lines 743-744: explicit scheme-test verification of factorization through the affine base open.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03FY (lemma-union-of-quasi-compact), with the affine-piece construction from Tag 03FX and open-image input Tag 06NF; final factorization written on scheme tests.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_atlas_open_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) : ∃ (I : Type u) (Xi : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (j : ∀ i : I, Xi i ⟶ X) (U : I → Over S) (a : ∀ i : I, yoneda.obj (U i) ⟶ (Xi i).obj.obj), IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (j i).hom.hom) ∧ ∀ i : I, IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (j i).hom.hom ∧ IsAffine (U i).left ∧ IsEtale (a i) ∧ IsSurjective (a i) ∧ ∃ W : S.Opens, IsAffine W.toScheme ∧ Nonempty ((Xi i).obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk W.ι))
